purpose: Implement the owner-approved canonical data classification as the single source of truth, map the three disagreeing classifications onto it, and record the ASVS consequences honestly.
requiredInvariants: The canonical schema is not bent to fit the existing lists; the existing lists are mapped onto it.
Every field name and every value rule carries exactly one canonical class.
No downstream control may drop a canonical class because its terminology differs, and a test asserts this per class and per outbound surface.
Coverage only widens: nothing previously redacted stops being redacted.
A term that is neither personal data nor a secret is not mislabelled as one to obtain coverage; it is denied by a separate, documented list.
Unspecified elements of the policy are recorded as open rather than invented.
An owner statement of sufficiency is authority over what the classification is, not evidence that an unwritten requirement exists.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database change; no migration or re-encryption.
acceptance: The code mirror and the approved schema agree on the class list, on outbound-redacted classes and on never-query-string classes, asserted by test.
Every outbound-redacted class is covered by at least one term, with the two prohibited classes excluded by name and on purpose.
Every term of every outbound-redacted class is proved redacted in the request body, in headers, in the query string and internally.
The policy document quotes every open item verbatim from the schema.
Three mutations were verified to turn the suite red: dropping a class from code, removing the last term of a class, and rewording an open item in one place only.
V14.1.2, V11.1.1 and V11.1.2 stay FAIL, each naming exactly what is still missing.
The evidence gate rejects 0 decisions; finalPass stays false.
